# Elliptic curves, Part II: Legendre interfaces

This Part II identifier indexes the seven Bennett–Siksek Legendre targets already planned by EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces. It imports that accepted plan’s equations, normalization, split readings of native descent, character-conductor interfaces, finite-field torsion and trace results without assigning duplicate declarations or planets. Its six layers are import records pending a maintainer merger; the owner’s mathematical layers remain planned with their existing gaps and supplier requests.

Use EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces as the single mathematical owner. The detailed document gives the source-to-owner crosswalk, imported APIs and tests, pinned conventions and remaining supplier obligations. No mathematical closure or completed merger is asserted.

stages.title: Legendre equations and root orderings
stages.description: Import LG.0 of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces. Over a commutative ring, Lλ has coefficients (0,−(1+λ),0,λ,0), and Ld,λ has (0,−d(1+λ),0,d²λ,0). Their discriminants are 16λ²(1−λ)² and 16d⁶λ²(1−λ)². Over a field with 2≠0, d≠0 and λ≠0,1 give ellipticity. Import normalization of full rational two-torsion to Ld,λ, the six labelled root-ordering parameters, the three root two-torsion points and exhaustion of the doubling kernel. The native twist parameters are (0,−d/4). These are imports of the owner’s 11 nodes, not new declarations.

stages.title: Good reduction and character conductors
stages.description: Import the five nodes of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.1. For F/Q elliptic with full rational two-torsion and semistable at odd primes, every associated λ and every odd good prime p satisfy v_p(λ)=v_p(1−λ)=0. The unscaled unit-parameter model has integral coefficients and unit discriminant over Z_p. For ω in {±1,±2}, the odd part of the primitive CA.1 character conductor of ωλ divides the actual elliptic conductor M of F, allowing character conductor 1. Minimal local models, primitive characters and actual conductor comparisons keep their existing suppliers and recorded obligations.

stages.title: Split-cubic readings of native descent
stages.description: Import the eight nodes of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.2 under 2≠0,d≠0,λ≠0,1. Evaluate the existing cubic algebra at roots (0,d,dλ) to identify it with K×K×K, and transport unit squareclasses. Read the existing native μ rather than constructing another descent: at a nonroot x it gives ([x],[x−d],[x−dλ]); at a root use the corrected derivative representative. All coordinate products are 1. A native affine point is twice a point iff its three x-differences are squares in K, with zero allowed only as a field square, not as a unit class.

stages.title: Two-primary torsion over prime fields
stages.description: Import the seven nodes of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.3. For prime p≡3 mod4 and η≠0,±1 in F_p, L_(η²)(F_p) contains Z/2×Z/4, so 8 divides its projective count. If i²=−1 in a field of characteristic other than two, (i,1−i) on L_(-1) doubles to (0,0) and has order four; its first descent class is [i]. At primes p≡5 mod8, only the zero-root two-torsion point is divisible, none of its halves is divisible, and v₂(pointCount L_(-1))=3. The exclusion of Z/4×Z/4 is retained.

stages.title: Corrected order-four point on the twist by two
stages.description: Import the four nodes of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.4. In a field with 2≠0, assume t,v≠0, i²=−1 and 2t²+2v²=1, and put λ=2t². The native point (2λ+4itv,8itv(t+iv)) on y²=x(x−2)(x−2λ) doubles to (2λ,0), has exact order four and third split descent class [4itv]. The correction is the existing source finding EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces/E1. The theorem is local algebra, independent of large-exponent progression assumptions.

stages.title: Trace and twist interfaces
stages.description: Import both nodes of EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.5. For prime p≡3 mod4 and u≠0 in F_p, y²=x(x−u)(x+u) has projective count p+1 and native trace zero. For odd p, d≠0 and λ≠0,1 in F_p, specialize the BSD.0 generic twist comparison to Ld,λ: its trace is quadraticChar(d) times that of Lλ, and its good Euler polynomial is 1−quadraticChar(d)a_p(Lλ)T+pT². For p≡5 mod8,d=2 this changes the sign. The generic comparison remains owned by BSD.0; these are equation-specific imports.
